#+property: header-args :tangle "~/.zshrc" :results silent
#+startup: content indent


* Introduction

This is the config I use for ZSH on my mac.  

(Reminder: {{M-x}} `org-babel-tangle` is
what genrates the output file until
things are set up to auto generate
on save.)


* Basics

** Edit Note


#+begin_src bash

  ## ----------------------------------------------
  ##
  ## DO NOTE EDIT THIS FIEL DIRECTLY
  ## 
  ## ~/.zshrc is maintained in
  ## ~/workshop/al9000.com/dotfiles/zshrc.org
  ## 
  ## ----------------------------------------------

#+end_src


** Turn On Prompt Expansion

#+begin_src bash

  setopt PROMPT_SUBST

#+end_src


** Turn On autocd

This sets up so you don't have to type ``cd`` to
move into a directory. 


#+begin_src bash

  setopt autocd 
  
#+end_src


** Don't Log Space Commands 

This prevents commands that start with a space
from being recorded in the command line log. 

WARNING: Don't rely on this for security. It's
too easy to forget to put a space in. I basically
never use this, but like it being there for
the once in a blue moon times when I find
it useful. 

#+begin_src bash

  setopt HIST_IGNORE_SPACE

#+end_src

** Set up/down arrows based on existing text

#+begin_src bash

  bindkey '^[[A' up-line-or-search
  bindkey '^[[B' down-line-or-search

#+end_src


** Use vim bindings

#+begin_src bash

  bindkey -v

#+end_src


* Display

** Prompt Colors and Vars

Sets up the variables used to make
the dynamic prompt. 

#+begin_src bash

  BG_ON='%K{233}'
  BG_OFF='%k'
  FG_ON='%F{#6b560e}'
  FG_OFF='%f'
  FG_CARET='%F{242}'
  FG_DOT='%F{239}'
  FG_OK='%F{22}'
  FG_ER='%F{124}'
  NEWLINE=$'\n'
  
#+end_src


** Colors for the `ls` Command

The default colors for some of the themes I use
don't read well when using the `ls` command.
This sets them to some explicit values based
off the ASCII Color table.

Probably messes with some themes (guessing
light mode themes specifically).

#+begin_src bash

  export CLICOLOR=1
  export LS_COLORS='di=1:fi=34:ln=31:pi=5:so=5:bd=5:cd=5:or=31'

#+end_src

* Prompt Functions

These functions are used to generate a dynamic CLI prompt.

** Last Status

Output a green OK or a red ERROR based on the return
value of the last command. 

#+begin_src bash

  function prompt_previous_exit_code() {
      if [[ $? -eq 0 ]]; then
          echo " ${FG_DOT}· ${FG_OK}OK${FG_ON}"
      else
          echo " ${FG_DOT}· ${FG_ER}ERROR: $?${FG_ON}"
      fi 
  }

#+end_src

** Current Git Branch

Show the name of the current git branch if you're
in a repo. Otherwise, just output a separator dot. 

#+begin_src bash

  function prompt_git_branch() {
      BRANCH_NAME=$(git branch --show-current 2> /dev/null)
      if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
          echo -n " ${FG_DOT}· [$BRANCH_NAME]${FG_ON}"
      else
          echo -n "${FG_DOT}${FG_ON}"
      fi 
  }
  
#+end_src


** Python VENV

Indicate if you're in a Python VENV virtual
environmnet. 

#+begin_src bash
  
  function prompt_python_venv() {
      if [ -n "$VIRTUAL_ENV" ]; then 
          echo -n " ${FG_DOT}· VENV${FG_ON}"
      else
          echo -n "${FG_DOT}${FG_ON}"
      fi
  }

#+end_src


** Date String

Basic date output. 

#+begin_src bash

  function prompt_date_string() {
     echo " ${FG_DOT}· $(date "+%-I:%M%p" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
  }

#+end_src


** Domain Name For Streaming

This is from when I was streaming to put
my domain name on the command line so
folks could see it (both live and
in the VODs)

#+begin_src bash

  function bio_url() {
      echo " ${FG_DOT}· al9000.com"
  }

#+end_src

* Promot Setup


This is the function that assembles the prompt. A
few things are commented out right now. I play
around with them periodically. 


#+begin_src bash

  function precmd() {
     PROMPT_EXIT_STRING=$(prompt_previous_exit_code)
     L1="${FG_CARET}> ${FG_ON}dojo $(dirs)"
     L1="${L1}${PROMPT_EXIT_STRING}"
     L1="${L1}$(prompt_python_venv)"
     L1="${L1}$(prompt_git_branch)"
     # L1="${L1}$(bio_url)"
     # L1="${L1}$(prompt_date_string)"
     # CHARCOUNT=${#L1}
     # COLCOUNT=$(($(tput cols) * 1))
     # for i in $( seq 1 $(( COLCOUNT - CHARCOUNT + 70)) ); do L1="$L1 "; done
     L1="${L1} ${FG_DOT}${PROMPT_DATE_STRING}${FG_ON} "
     PS1="${L1}${NEWLINE}${FG_CARET}>${FG_OFF} "
  }
  
#+end_src

* Deprecated

** chruby

This is old as well as deprecated. Last
time I used Ruby, I used `rbenv` instead of
`chruby`. It's (also deprecated) setup is
listed below. 

#+begin_src bash :tangle no
  
  source $HOMEBREW_PREFIX/opt/chruby/share/chruby/chruby.sh 
  source $HOMEBREW_PREFIX/opt/chruby/share/chruby/auto.sh 
  chruby ruby-3.1.2

#+end_src


** rbenv


#+begin_src bash :tangle no

  eval "$(rbenv init - zsh)"

#+end_src


** nvm

I haven't done anything with nvm in a while. 
This is a weird line to get things to work.
Will re-examine it if I need to do nvm stuff
in the future to see if there's a more
susinct way. 


#+begin_src bash :tangle no

  export NVM_DIR="$([ -z "${XDG_CONFIG_HOME-}" ] && printf %s "${HOME}/.nvm" || printf %s "${XDG_CONFIG_HOME}/nvm")"
  [ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ] && \. "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" # This loads nvm

#+end_src
